crates/omv-syntax/src/markdown.rs:465 and :473 use text.get(start..end).unwrap_or_default() in emit(). Correct today -- the byte indices come from tokenize() scanning the same &str, and * / _ are ASCII so a run can never split a multi-byte char -- but the fallback turns a future tokenizer bug into silently dropped text rather than a visible failure, which is the exact class of defect the 'never loses text' DoD exists to prevent. unwrap() is correctly avoided per the ratchet; a debug_assert! on the slice being Some, or a small slice helper, would keep the invariant loud in tests without adding an unwrap.

Backslash escapes are not honoured: 'text with a\\*escaped\\* star' renders as 'text with a\\escaped\\ star' with the middle span styled Italic. The backslashes survive but the author's escaped asterisks are consumed as emphasis delimiters, so intentionally-literal text is restyled and two characters change meaning. Not malformed input, so the spec's 'never loses/mutates buffer text' degradation rule does not reach it, and escapes are not in REQ-002's v1 construct list -- accepted as out of v1 scope, recorded as the one input class where rendered output diverges from author intent.

heading() and horizontal_rule() call trim_start()/trim() and discard the leading indentation: '   # x' renders as '# x' and '  ----------' renders as a rule with no leading blank columns. list_item() by contrast preserves indentation inside the marker span (asserted by ordered_and_unordered_items_keep_a_marker for '  - nested'). The asymmetry is undocumented and untested in either direction, so a later reader cannot tell which is intended. Cosmetic only; no line is lost.

a_stray_emphasis_marker_stays_literal_text covers '_' alone on a line (stays literal) but not '*' alone, which takes a different path: render("*") produces a ListMarker span '• ' (bullet plus trailing space), since a bare - / * / + is an empty list item before it is a stray emphasis marker. Same for '-' and '1.'. Defensible and CommonMark-consistent, but the divergence between the two markers is exactly what the test name promises to pin and does not.

toggling_on_records_the_focused_window_and_off_clears_it (crates/omv/src/main.rs) exercises the DoD's 'regardless of which window is focused' only in the off direction. The assertion has real teeth against a first_id() bug but would not catch a last_id()/newest-window bug. Adding a second ':md' toggle-on after focus has moved to the left window, asserting Some(left), would make the on direction symmetric. The anti-per-frame-parse grep guard "! grep -qE 'markdown::(\{[^}]*, *)?render' crates/omv/src/ui.rs" enforces a real boundary and does catch every realistic form -- I probed markdown::render(x), omv_syntax::markdown::render(x), use omv_syntax::markdown::render;, and use omv_syntax::{MarkdownLine, markdown::render}; all CAUGHT. But three equivalent forms slip past: markdown::{render} and markdown::{ render } (the alternation requires a comma inside the braces, so a single-item brace import is MISSED) and use omv_syntax::markdown::*; followed by a bare render(..) (MISSED). Since ui.rs today contains no occurrence of the substring 'markdown::' at all (its only references are app.markdown_for and theme.markdown_style), the strictly tighter and simpler guard "! grep -q 'markdown::' crates/omv/src/ui.rs" would close all three gaps with no false positives. Low severity -- the evasions are contrived and the guard covers the shortcut a hurried implementer would actually take.

refresh_markdown_pane runs at the end of EVERY effect batch, so while the pane is visible a pure motion (j, h, Esc, each character of a : command line) re-parses the whole document - the counter test proves it: 'entering insert mode is one effect batch' asserts +1 parse for a keystroke that changes no text. The doc comment at app.rs:860-862 calls this 'the same cost class CLAUDE.md already accepts for tree-sitter/LSP full-document sync', but refresh_highlights_for is strictly narrower: it fires on Effect::BufferChanged, open_path, and focus_window only, never on a bare motion. Accepted for this task because the plan specified once-per-batch, but the precedent claim is overstated and a dirty-flag (buffer index + rope revision) would restore parity.

CLAUDE.md as committed at 771648b contained two doc errors, both corrected at 36f1357 (correction verified accurate by review). (1) It named a type that does not exist, omv-syntax::markdown::Renderer; the real API is the free function 'pub fn render(text: &str) -> Vec<MarkdownLine>' at crates/omv-syntax/src/markdown.rs:125. (2) It wrote that 'exact line-for-line correspondence is not required, since markup collapses the line count', inverting the load-bearing invariant: render() returns exactly one MarkdownLine per source line, which is precisely why the pane reuses window.scroll untouched and needs no scroll machinery. Verified every_source_line_produces_exactly_one_rendered_line at markdown.rs:824 asserts render(source).len() == source.split('\n').count() across 8 inputs (empty, bare newline, no trailing newline, CRLF, unclosed fence), i.e. a derived count, not a fixed number.

ROOT SOURCE of finding #27 is the APPROVED SPEC, not the SWE. overview.md REQ-005 says 'exact line-for-line correspondence is not required, since raw and rendered line counts can differ', and the non-goals list at overview.md:106-109 repeats it: 'collapsed markup (**bold** -> bold) makes raw and rendered line counts differ'. That rationale is factually false -- collapsing happens WITHIN a line, never across lines. The SWE copied the spec faithfully. The implementation delivers a strictly STRONGER guarantee (exact 1:1) and its correctness DEPENDS on it: ui.rs:380-383 indexes the markdown cache with window.scroll directly. Consequence: the approved spec is now the stale artifact, and a maintainer optimising the parser to satisfy only REQ-005-as-written could collapse lines, still satisfy the spec, and silently misalign the panes. Tightening REQ-005 is a spec change and needs renewed human confirmation; NOT rewritten by review.

The six floor-agreement checks in task-07 are self-referential and pass unchanged at the parent commit cd725c9 (verified in a worktree): 'pre-push floor == ci floor', the two harness.md row greps, the CLAUDE.md '-ge 2' count, and the README number grep all PASS at 83/83. They detect a PARTIAL update but cannot detect a wrong-but-consistent number. The only reality-anchored check is 'measured -ge floor', and -ge permits an under-set floor (floor=100 would have passed every check). Compensating control is reviewer measurement, which the task Notes correctly anticipated. Independently re-measured with CI's own summation via rtk proxy (the local rtk hook collapses cargo test output and makes the sed yield 0 -- an environment artifact, not a CI one): RAW SUM = 127, exactly equal to the floor, not merely above it.

MINOR, not blocking. Two README omissions in the new '## Markdown render' section. (1) The pane silently does not draw when the carved rect is too small: ui.rs:98 returns None if raw.width == 0 || pane.width < MARKDOWN_MIN (3) || pane.height < MARKDOWN_MIN, so on a narrow window the toggle appears to do nothing while the flag is on. Undocumented. (2) REQ-006's extension-agnostic behaviour is a deliberate, tested feature (the_render_pane_ignores_the_files_extension, crates/omv/src/main.rs:871) but the README never says the pane works on any buffer regardless of extension; a reader would reasonably assume it is gated on .md. Neither is a false claim, so neither is a defect in the strict sense.
